title: Token pacing and kernel backpressure proto
content:
Context and motivation:

This note collects an experimental proposal for reducing tail latency induced by KV cache paging and long-running fused kernels (FlashAttention + quantized GEMM combos) when sequence length distributions are heavy-tailed. We call the approach watermark-based token pacing + kernel backpressure. The goal is to keep mean cost low with predictable 99/99.9 latency while preserving batching benefits for throughput.

Problem statement (observed):
- Long sequences or cold KV pages cause some requests to incur multi-ms stalls while a prefetch + fused kernel finishes; other requests in the same warp/SM can be delayed because we keep large batch windows open.
- Traditional batching accumulators wait for either token budget or time-slice; with paged KV we get janky outliers when a few requests trigger disk/pinned-memory hydration.
- Existing heuristics (max-batch-size, sequence bucketing) help but do not react to in-flight kernel health or paged-KV residency fraction. We need a lightweight kernel-facing backpressure signal and a scheduler policy that paces token admission across requests.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Watermark-based token pacing: maintain two per-tenant watermarks (soft, hard) that bound the number of inflight tokens across all kernels. New token admission is throttled if the soft watermark is reached; only allow hedged or high-priority requests to exceed up to the hard watermark.

2) Kernel-level backpressure primitive: augment kernel launch contract with a tiny host-visible progress/credit counter (32-bit atomic in pinned page or small UCX message). Kernels periodically write progress (tokens emitted or work units completed). The scheduler can read counters to detect slow kernels and reduce admission or trigger preempt/fallback.

3) Residency-aware kernel variant selection: dispatch one of three kernel classes based on estimated KV residency fraction for the request window:
   - Hot-resident fast path: fully fused FlashAttention+quant-kernel optimized for in-memory KV (minimal prefetch).
   - Mixed-residency hybrid kernel: emits intermediate progress and cooperates with prefetch worker (split pipeline).
   - Cold-resident safe path: non-blocking incremental kernel that yields after small work-chunks allowing other streams to progress.

4) Micro-SLA hedging: for requests near SLO breach (based on in-flight latency estimate), spawn a lightweight fallback kernel on cheaper capacity or run a shallow decode short-circuit that returns partial output and schedules full decode in background.

Scheduler proto (pseudo):

state: global_inflight_tokens, soft_watermark, hard_watermark, per-kernel-progress[]

on_request(req):
  tokens = estimate_remaining_tokens(req)
  if global_inflight_tokens + tokens > hard_watermark:
    if req.priority == "high": allow but mark stat 'hard-exceed'
    else: queue req into admission-queue
  elif global_inflight_tokens + tokens > soft_watermark:
    if is_high_latency_risk(req): select fallback path or small-batch kernel
    else: admit with pacing_hint = true
  else:
    admit normal

on_kernel_progress_update(kernel_id, progress_delta):
  per-kernel-progress[kernel_id] += progress_delta
  if progress_rate(kernel_id) < slow_threshold:
    // detect long-running/paged workload
    mark kernel_id slow
    reduce admission for requests using same KV cohort
    optionally push eviction/prioritized prefetch for that cohort

Kernel contract additions (minimal changes):
- launch args: {max_tokens_budget, kv_cohort_id, prefetch_hint, pacing_hint}
- kernel heartbeat: write atomic progress every N emitted tokens (N ~ 16-64, tunable)
- early-yield return code: K_YIELDED to signal scheduler to reschedule remaining work later
- metrics hooks: total GPU-time, wait-for-prefetch-time, progress_rate

Implementation sketch:
- Heartbeat mechanism: small pinned host page per GPU SM group with preallocated 64-bit slots. Kernels update with atomic add; host polls on a light cadence (10-50Hz) or receives UCX push for scale. Use single-writer multiple-reader safely since only kernel updates its slot.
- Kernel variants: maintain a link-time table of kernel function pointers; dispatcher picks variant based on kv_residency_estimator (hot fraction from profiler or recent hits). Keep binary size controlled by linking only a small set of param-specializations.
- Prefetch worker: when scheduler notices slow kernel, it escalates prefetch for the cohort with higher priority and throttles new admissions. Prefetch duplicates are limited by cohort concurrency budget.

Tuning knobs and heuristics:
- soft_watermark ~= average_inflight_tokens + 1.5 * stdev; hard_watermark =~ average + 4*stdev (start conservative)
- heartbeat interval: smaller values give faster detection but higher overhead. 32-token heartbeat seems a good starting point.
- progress_rate slow_threshold: empirical; start at 20% of median for similar batch size
- kv_cohort grouping key: model + sequence_length_bucket + user_tenant + top_k_active_prefix_hash

Experiment plan (quick A/B):
1) Baseline: current batching with sequence bucketing across mixed workload (synthetic heavy-tail + normal mixes)
2) Implement admission controller + soft/hard watermarks (no kernel heartbeat) — measure 99/99.9 latency and throughput
3) Add kernel heartbeat + detection + simple throttling — measure tail improvements and false throttles
4) Add kernel variants dispatch (hot/mixed/cold) and prefetch escalation — compare cost and latency
5) Run with micro-SLA hedging enabled on a subset of requests to evaluate user-visible tradeoffs

Metrics to collect:
- p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency for decode step and end-to-end request
- extra GPU-seconds per request (cost delta)
- number of K_YIELDED events and reschedules per request
- KV prefetch bandwidth and duplicated prefetch ratio
- false positive slow detections (kernels marked slow but recover quickly)

Risks and open questions:
- Kernel heartbeat adds a tiny atomic cost and pinned memory bandwidth; need to measure contention at scale across 8-16 SM groups per GPU.
- Early-yield re-scheduling complexity: we must ensure MV semantics for KV state and rehydrate minimal context to resume. Can add a resume token in the kernel contract.
- Prefetch duplication might increase bandwidth cost; need cohort-level budgets and dedupe heuristics.
- Complexity vs benefit: incremental rollout recommended (start with soft-watermark admission, then heartbeat, then kernel variants).

Short-term next steps (owners):
- Prototype admission controller in runtime scheduler (Diego) — 2w
- Minimal kernel heartbeat stub in fused-attn kernel (Priya) — 1w
- Simple experiment harness to replay heavy-tail seq mixes (Maya) — 1w
- Postmortem template for long-tail requests instrumenting kernel progress (Liam) — 1w

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Check interactions with current prefix/KV caching eviction logic and eviction-triggered cold fetch path.
- Add diagnostic view in Console: per-cohort inflight tokens + heartbeat rates to explain throttling.
- Consider using small SM-local ring buffers and a single aggregator to reduce pinned atomics when scaling to multi-GPU per-host setups.

References / inspiration:
- FlashAttention perf patterns (internal profiler traces)
- Prior art: admission control in network stacks (watermarks) and cooperative multitasking kernels

End.
